Go to **Data → Forecast Sheet**.\n4. Choose line chart.\n5. Set **Forecast End** to some future date (e.g., 3–6 months ahead).\n6. Click **Options**:\n   - Check that **“Seasonality”** is detected. If not, set it manually to **7** (weekly pattern).\n7. Click **Create**.\n\nExcel will create a new sheet (e.g., `Forecast_Total`) with:\n\n- Historical totals\n- Forecasted totals\n- Upper/lower bounds\n\nRepeat the same process using **Phone**, **Chat**, and **Email** columns instead of Total to get channel‑level forecasts.\n\nThis alone gives you a solid baseline.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Add manual holiday adjustments (simple but powerful)\n\nExcel’s ETS might not fully capture *spiky* restaurant holidays yet, because you only have one season of some dates. You can overlay a simple adjustment.\n\n1. On each forecast sheet (e.g., `Forecast_Total`), find the rows that are holidays (match forecast dates to your **Holidays** sheet).\n2. For each holiday:\n   - Look at last year’s actual (if you have it yet; for some you will, for some you won’t).\n   - Compare normal “like” days around it.\n\nExample approach on separate sheet **Holiday_Uplift**:\n\n- Columns: Date, UpliftFactor\n- If a normal Friday is 1,000 contacts and last Valentine’s Day (Friday) was 1,600 → UpliftFactor \u003d 1.6\n\nOn the forecast sheet, add a column:\n\n- **HolidayFactor**:\n  ```excel\n  \u003dIFERROR(\n     INDEX(Holiday_Uplift[UpliftFactor],\n       MATCH([@[ForecastDate]], Holiday_Uplift[Date], 0)\n     ),\n     1\n  )\n  ```\n- **AdjustedForecast**:\n  ```excel\n  \u003d[@Forecast] * [@HolidayFactor]\n  ```\n\nNow your holiday days get boosted or reduced appropriately.\n\n---\n\n## 6. If it’s weekly, the logic is the same, just change “day” → “week”.\n\n---\n\n### 1. Set up your base data tab\n\n1. Put *all* data in one table on a sheet called **Raw_Data**:\n   - **A:** Date\n   - **B:** Channel (Chat / Phone / Email)\n   - **C:** Volume (contacts)\n\n   Make sure **Date** is a real date (not text).\n\n2. Turn it into an Excel Table:\n   - Click anywhere in the data → **Ctrl+T** → “My table has headers.”\n\n---\n\n### 2. Build a clean daily summary by channel\n\nCreate a new sheet **Daily_Summary**.\n\n1. In row 1 create headers like:\n   - **A1:** Date  \n   - **B1:** Phone  \n   - **C1:** Chat  \n   - **D1:** Email  \n   - **E1:** Total\n\n2. In **A2**, list your dates (one per day, no gaps). For each channel, use `SUMIFS`:\n\n   In **B2** (Phone volume for that date), then copy down:\n   ```excel\n   \u003dSUMIFS(Raw_Data[Volume], Raw_Data[Date], $A2, Raw_Data[Channel], \"Phone\")\n   ```\n\n   In **C2** (Chat):\n   ```excel\n   \u003dSUMIFS(Raw_Data[Volume], Raw_Data[Date], $A2, Raw_Data[Channel], \"Chat\")\n   ```\n\n   In **D2** (Email):\n   ```excel\n   \u003dSUMIFS(Raw_Data[Volume], Raw_Data[Date], $A2, Raw_Data[Channel], \"Email\")\n   ```\n\n4. In **E2** (Total daily contacts), then copy down:\n   ```excel\n   \u003dSUM(B2:D2)\n   ```\n\n---\n\n### 3. Add calendar \u0026 seasonality fields\n\nOn **Daily_Summary**, add these helper columns:\n\n- **F:** DayOfWeek  \n  ```excel\n  \u003dTEXT(A2,\"ddd\")   \u0027 or \"dddd\" for full name\n  ```\n\n- **G:** WeekNumber  \n  ```excel\n  \u003dWEEKNUM(A2,2)\n  ```\n\n- **H:** Month  \n  ```excel\n  \u003dTEXT(A2,\"mmm\")\n  ```\n\n- **I:** Year  \n  ```excel\n  \u003dYEAR(A2)\n  ```\n\n- **J:** IsHoliday (flag major restaurant days)\n  - Create a small **Holidays** sheet (Date + HolidayName).\n  - Then use:\n    ```excel\n    \u003dIF(COUNTIF(Holidays!$A:$A, A2)\u003e0, 1, 0)\n    ```\n\nYou can also add flags like **IsWeekend**, **IsDayBeforeHoliday**, etc., if you want more refinement later.\n\n---\n\n### 4. Create a simple custom seasonal forecast (if you want more control)\n\nThis is a common WFM trick when you have holidays/seasonality:\n\n#### 5.1. Build “like day” averages\n\nOn a new sheet **Patterns**:\n\n1. Create a small table of **Average volume by DayOfWeek and Month** (and optionally by Channel).\n\n   Example headers:\n   - **A:** Month\n   - **B:** DayOfWeek\n   - **C:** Avg_Total\n   - **D:** Avg_Phone\n   - **E:** Avg_Chat\n   - **F:** Avg_Email\n\n2. Build holiday uplift factors\n\nOn sheet **Holiday_Uplift**:\n\n1. For each holiday (e.g., Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, Christmas Eve, NYE):\n   - List **HolidayName**, **Date**, **Channel**, **ActualVolume**, and **BaselineVolume** for that same day-of-week/month in a “normal” period.\n2. Click **Options**:\n   - Check seasonality. If you’re using **daily data**, Excel might auto-detect. For weekly patterns over the year:\n     - Weekly data: set seasonality to around **52** (weeks per year).\n     - Daily data: seasonality of **7** for weekly pattern; **365** if you have multiple years and Excel supports it.\n5. Click **Create**.\n\nExcel will:\n- Create a new sheet with:\n  - **Historical \u0026 forecast values**\n  - **Upper/lower confidence bounds**\n- Use Exponential Smoothing (ETS), which handles seasonality decently.\n\nRepeat for **Chat**, **Email**, and **Total**.\n\n---\n\n### 5. Create a simple custom seasonal forecast (if you want more control)\n\nThis is a common WFM trick when you have holidays/seasonality:\n\n#### 5.1. Build “like day” averages\n\nOn a new sheet **Patterns**:\n\n1. Create a small table of **Average volume by DayOfWeek and Month** (and optionally by Channel).\n\n   Example headers:\n   - **A:** Month\n   - **B:** DayOfWeek\n   - **C:** Avg_Total\n   - **D:** Avg_Phone\n   - **E:** Avg_Chat\n   - **F:** Avg_Email\n\n2. Use a PivotTable:\n   - Insert → PivotTable from **Daily_Summary**.\n   - Rows: Month, then DayOfWeek.\n   - Values: Average of Total, Phone, Chat, Email.\n\n   Copy the pivot results into your **Patterns** table so you have static numbers you can reference.\n\n#### 5.2. Build holiday uplift factors\n\nOn sheet **Holiday_Uplift**:\n\n1. For each holiday (e.g., Valentine’s Day, Mother’s Day, Christmas Eve, NYE):\n   - List **HolidayName**, **Date**, **Channel**, **ActualVolume**, and **BaselineVolume** for that same day-of-week/month in a “normal” period.\n2. Compute a **UpliftFactor**:\n   ```excel\n   \u003dActualVolume / BaselineVolume\n   ```\n   So if you usually get 1,000 total contacts but Valentine’s Day had 1,800, uplift \u003d **1.8**.\n\nYou can build just a short list of key restaurant holidays; that’s often enough.\n\n---\n\n### 6. Build your Forecast sheet\n\nCreate a new sheet **Forecast**.\n\n1. In columns:\n   - **A:** Date (future days you want to forecast)\n   - **B:** DayOfWeek (`\u003dTEXT(A2,\"ddd\")`)\n   - **C:** Month (`\u003dTEXT(A2,\"mmm\")`)\n   - **D:** IsHoliday (via the **Holidays** sheet, same as earlier)\n   - **E:** Baseline_Total\n   - **F:** HolidayFactor\n   - **G:** Forecast_Total\n   - Add similar for Phone, Chat, Email if needed.\n\n2. **Baseline_Total** from Patterns (Month + DayOfWeek):\n\n   Assuming your **Patterns** table is named `PatternsTbl` with columns [Month], [DayOfWeek], [Avg_Total]:\n\n   In **E2**:\n   ```excel\n   \u003dINDEX(PatternsTbl[Avg_Total],\n      MATCH(1,\n           (PatternsTbl[Month]\u003d$C2)*\n           (PatternsTbl[DayOfWeek]\u003d$B2),\n      0)\n   )\n   ```\n   Confirm as an array formula in older Excel (Ctrl+Shift+Enter) or just Enter in 365/2021. Then copy down.\n\n3. **HolidayFactor**:\n\n   On **Holiday_Uplift**, suppose you have `Holiday_Uplift[Date]` and `Holiday_Uplift[UpliftFactor]`.\n\n   In **F2**:\n   ```excel\n   \u003dIFERROR(\n     INDEX(Holiday_Uplift[UpliftFactor],\n       MATCH($A2, Holiday_Uplift[Date], 0)\n     ),\n     1\n   )\n   ```\n   So normal days get factor 1; holidays get their uplift.\n\n4. **Forecast_Total**:\n\n   In **G2**:\n   ```excel\n   \u003dE2 * F2\n   ```\n\nRepeat for **Phone**, **Chat**, **Email** using channel-specific averages and uplift factors if you have them.\n\n---\n\n### 7. Turn forecasts into staffing-ready views\n\nOnce **Forecast** is built:\n\n- Add columns for **Interval distribution** (e.g., % of daily contacts by hour) if you staff by intraday.\n- Create PivotTables/Charts:\n  - Forecast by **week**, **channel**, and **holiday**.\n  - Compare **this year vs last year** for sanity checks.\n\n---\n\n### 8. High‑Level Product Requirements\n\nMain references:\n- **2026 – AI Assisted Returns – High Level Requirements** (Tech wiki).  \n- **2026 – AI Assisted Returns – Product Brief** (Product wiki).  \n- **AI Assisted Returns — Business Requirements Document v2** (partner‑facing BRD).  \n\n**Problem / Opportunity**  \n- Current **Return Portal** is a multi‑page, self‑service flow that feels rigid vs. merchants’ conversational CX.  \n- Merchant chatbots cannot call into Happy Returns’ eligibility rules, inventory, and methods, forcing duplicated or brittle workflows.  \n- There’s lost opportunity to:\n  - Reduce support load.\n  - Proactively drive exchanges / revenue recapture.\n  - Differentiate via agentic, conversational returns.\n\n**Chosen solution direction**  \n1. **Happy Returns–Managed Returns Flow Agent API (Recommended, Phase 1)**  \n   - New API/MCP layer that programmatically navigates the existing Return Portal logic (eligibility, methods, fees, etc.) while bypassing the UI.  \n   - Exposes an **OpenAPI spec and/or MCP tools** so external agents can integrate with minimal custom work.  \n2. **Happy Returns Embeddable Agent (Phase 2 option)**  \n   - JavaScript widget/chatbot using the same Agent API, embeddable directly on merchant sites; deferred to later phase.  \n3. **AI inside the existing Portal (deprioritized)**  \n   - Seen as less compelling vs. copy/design improvements and not the primary focus.  \n\nOut of scope for this initiative: **building a Happy Returns‑branded chatbot UI, new return types/custom per‑merchant logic, and generic headless returns integration.**  \n\n---\n\n### 3. Detailed Functional Flow \u0026 Tooling\n\nThe BRD and HLR converge on a **sequential tool-based flow** backed by MCP, with strong state management and agent guidance.  \n\n**Core conversation flow (MVP)**\n\n1. **Initialize \u0026 Authenticate Shopper**\n   - OAuth2 auth into HR’s MCP server for the partner.  \n   - Shopper auth using existing portal methods (order + ZIP, email, etc.), with clear error handling for not found / invalid details.  \n\n2. **Get Order Details / Eligibility**  \n   - Tool: **Get Order Details / get_purchases**.  \n   - Returns orders, items, images, SKU/UPC, prices, and **item‑level return eligibility** based on merchant rules (windows, final sale, already returned, etc.).  \n\n3. **Select Item(s)**  \n   - Tool: **Select Item**.  \n   - Shopper (via agent) chooses which item(s) to return; output is eligible refund methods per item.  \n\n4. **Select Refund Method**  \n   - Tool: **Select Refund Method / get_refund_methods**.  \n   - MVP supports **Refund to original payment** and **Store Credit**; exchanges, return shopping, etc. are **post‑MVP**.  \n\n5. **Select Drop‑Off Method**  \n   - Tool: **Select Drop‑off Method / get_dropoff_methods**.  \n   - MVP methods: **Return Bar** and **Mail** only.  \n   - Must provide **closest Return Bar locations** and a locator link in responses.  \n\n6. **Preview \u0026 Confirm Return**  \n   - Tool: **preview_return**.  \n   - Show summary of items, methods, refund types, fees, any site credit bonuses, before submission.  \n\n7. **Start Return \u0026 Deliver Outputs**  \n   - Tool: **start_return**.  \n   - Outputs:\n     - QR codes and/or mail labels.\n     - Clear shopper‑facing drop‑off instructions.\n     - Link/redirect to **Return Status** page; email communications handled by HR.  \n\n8. **Utility Tools**\n   - **Reset Flow**: restart conversation \u0026 state.  \n   - **Get Return Bars**: dedicated tool for closest locations (used in various flow points).  \n\n**State \u0026 safety requirements**\n\n- Every tool call must return **state metadata** (currentStep, maxSteps, previousTool, nextTool, allowedTools). Calls to tools outside `allowedTools` must be rejected.  \n- Each response includes **agentInstructions**: concrete copy/constraints to drive the partner’s chatbot prompts and ensure explicit shopper confirmation between steps.  \n\n---\n\n### 4. Scope, Phasing, and Integrations\n\n**Phase 1 (Birdy Grey / Forethought pilot focus)**  \n\n- Platforms: **Shopify** only (others “nice to have”).  \n- Return Functionality: **Refunds + Site Credit** (no exchanges or return shopping yet).  \n- Methods: **Return Bar + Mail**.  \n- Integrations targeted: Forethought, Gladly, Zendesk, Gorgias, Cavalry etc. with shared partner‑facing docs by ~**2/13** and feedback by **week of 2/20**.  \n\n**Post‑MVP**  \n\n- Additional integrations: **BigCommerce, StandardAPI, Headless**, etc.  \n- Features: **Exchanges, return shopping, gift returns, returnless refunds, non‑consolidated methods, shopper‑provided labels**.  \n\n**Go‑to‑Market \u0026 Partner Requirements**  \n\n- HR must **review and approve** partner chatbot flows (staging/demo env) before launch.  \n- Must demonstrate:\n  - Shopper auth,\n  - Eligible/ineligible scenarios,\n  - Return creation,\n  - Error handling.  \n- Partners are responsible for **secure storage and handling of PII** inside their systems; HR is not responsible for PII in partner‑managed chat UIs or tooling.  \n\n---\n\n### 5. Architecture \u0026 Engineering Requirements\n\n**Core architecture direction**\n\n- New Go service: **`returns-mcp-server`**.  \n- Integrations:\n  - **AWS Cognito OAuth2** for chatbot auth.\n  - **Redis** for session management.\n  - **MCP handler** (JSON‑RPC / HTTP) that wraps returns‑app APIs.  \n- Rate limiting tuned for MCP fan‑out (multiple shoppers behind one MCP IP), with possible special casing or removal of certain rate limits for MCP traffic.  \n- Mark returns in data as **“started via AI agents”** in Dynamo via returns‑service/data‑castle, so downstream reporting and (optionally) dashboards/APIs can distinguish them.  \n\n**MCP vs OpenAPI discussion**\n\n- Early sizing and RFC threads discussed:\n  - **Low‑lift OpenAPI‑only approach** (export spec from existing REST APIs).  \n  - **Dedicated MCP server** for richer, deterministic tooling and better partner ecosystem alignment.  \n- Consensus has moved toward **MCP‑first with optional REST/OpenAPI later**:\n  - MCP has strong ecosystem adoption and bidirectional registration semantics that improve tool reliability.  \n  - Supporting both is considered a manageable extension once MCP server is in place.  \n\n**Tech components \u0026 readiness**  \n\n- **Foundation**: service scaffolding, auth, sessions, MCP handler.  \n- **Core tools \u0026 flow tools**: the specific MCP methods listed above.  \n- **Production readiness**:  \n  - Rate‑limiting, error handling, observability (metrics/logs/traces), runbooks.  \n  - Security review (Veracode + possible extra pen‑testing).  \n  - BI work (dbt + Looker) to surface AI‑started returns.  \n\n---\n\n### 6. Reporting \u0026 Metrics Requirements\n\n**Operational \u0026 behavior metrics**  \n\n- **Interactions**:\n  - Total chatbot sessions initiated.\n  - Session abandonment.  \n- **Return outcomes**:\n  - Number of returns started via chatbot.  \n  - Shopper return completion time (first API call → label/QR generated).  \n  - Return drop‑off time (label/QR issued → drop‑off).  \n- **Reliability**:\n  - API error rate (4xx/5xx on Agent API).  \n  - Escalations to live agents.  \n- **Business KPIs**:\n  - Maintain or improve **Return Bar adoption**, **revenue retention**, **NPS**, and **merchant adoption** (merchants launched and volume of AI‑started returns within 3 months).  \n\n**Data modeling \u0026 exposure**\n\n- Store AI‑started indicator in **Dynamo return record**, log to **AES**, then expose via BI/dbt/Looker for internal reporting.  \n- There is ongoing discussion about:\n  - Whether to also surface this flag in **retailer dashboards, partner APIs and webhooks** (post‑MVP, requires design + extra work).  \n  - Whether additional external reporting via APIs/webhooks is needed or if existing reporting is sufficient for now.  \n\n---\n\n### 7. Estimates, Status, and Key Discussions\n\n**Estimates \u0026 sizing**\n\n- Initial technical estimates from the HLR doc sum to **~2.75 CF sprints + extra line items** (BI \u0026 Security) plus **1 sprint buffer** for internal testing/refinement.  \n- RFC discussion in `#hpy-eng-rfc` converged on **“~6 ± 1 sprints”** overall to be safe, accounting for scope expansion and internal iteration.  \n- Separate Jira items track:\n  - **Sizing spike** NTK‑1261 (“Sizing Estimate for AI Assisted Agent”).  \n  - **Provide HLE for AI assisted returns** CF‑6710.  \n  - **Return Flow MCP – High Level Architecture Proposal** AG‑221.  \n\n**Key discussion threads**\n\n- **Project sizing \u0026 approach** – `#hpy-sales-enablement-intake-process` (t‑shirt sizing, OpenAPI vs MCP, leveraging existing integration specs).  \n- **Estimation reviews** – `#hpy-dev-only-consumerflow` and `#hpy-eng-rfc` (debating optimism of estimates, adding buffer, BI/Security scope, storage of AI‑started flag).  \n- **Partner coordination \u0026 BRD** – `#hpy-ai-assisted-returns` (partner‑facing doc, timelines, coordination with Forethought/Gladly/Gorgias/Cavalry, BRD v2 shared on 2/13).  \n\n---\n\n### 8.
